entries.words: A neutral developer-tool style: grey text roles on white or near-black, translucent grey for hover and active, a muted green as the one brand colour and a five-step severity ramp from neutral through low, medium and high to critical, each lighter in dark mode. Small text gets its own three steps for dense panels. Layers are named so overlays stack in one agreed order.

entries.words: Warm stone greys from near-white to near-black with one strong accent, a Swiss red by default, used sparingly for a rule, a link or a single action. Text steps down by opacity of one ink rather than by new greys. The source allows steps at 40% and 20% opacity; those fail the contrast floor for text and are left out here, kept only for rules and disabled states.

display.fontFamily: a plex-class grotesk; free stand-in IBM Plex Sans

entries.words: Large display type at a light weight, set solid and tracked in a little, with headings that stay light and body text on a 60-character measure. Emphasis is medium, never bold. It reads as modern and exact, and needs a family with a true light weight; a system fallback without one turns it heavy.

entries.words: A strict twelve-column page on an 8px unit where content takes eight columns and supporting matter takes four, sections separated by large, regular gaps. The asymmetry carries the hierarchy without boxes or colour. Pitfall: at 768 the four-column side drops below the eight; give it an order that still reads.

entries.words: A text-only first screen: a small spaced label, a short accent rule, a light headline and a lead on a narrow measure, then a solid and an outlined button, with a huge pale section numeral behind at the top right. It gives a sober page a single graphic move. The numeral is decoration and must not compete with the headline's contrast.

entries.words: An industrial palette with two grounds, a near-black and a warm cream, a mid grey for secondary text on the dark ground, a very dark green as a third ground, and one hot orange held under about a sixth of any screen. Corners are square or nearly so, and controls answer quickly while sections reveal slowly. Pitfall: grey and orange on the cream ground fail the contrast floor for text and are left out; orange carries text only on the dark ground, or sits as a fill under dark text.

entries.words: A site scale drawn from measurement rather than taste: the source read 202 sites at 1440 and 390 and found the first headline near 72px on desktop and 40px on a phone, about four times the body size, with generous section gaps. This entry turns that into a fluid display size, body text a little above 16px, and margins that grow with the screen.

entries.words: One tab model that shows as a bottom tab bar on a phone and as a sectioned sidebar on a tablet or desktop, with each tab owning its own navigation stack. Some sections appear only in the sidebar, and a compose tab opens a sheet rather than switching. It keeps one structure across sizes instead of two shells.

entries.words: A chat or capture screen whose input bar sits in the bottom safe area outside the scrolling list, so it rides above the keyboard and never scrolls away. Dragging the list dismisses the keyboard. It is the shape of any screen whose main act is typing into a stream.

entries.words: A React Native shell that keeps one set of tabs and moves them from the bottom to the left at 768 wide, either as a full sidebar or a compact icon rail with labels beneath. A drawer can follow the same rule, permanent on wide screens and over the content on narrow ones. It suits an app that ships to phones and tablets from one codebase.

entries.words: The frame of a web app added to the home screen and run without browser chrome: the page draws under a translucent status bar, the safe-area insets are mirrored into variables once, the header grows by the top inset and the bottom navigation by the bottom one, and the root element owns the scroll so overscroll does not drag the whole app. The top inset may be zero; never assume it.
